title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from neighbouring pages). E is an elliptic curve over a field k of characteristic ≠ 2. F_n = H^0(E, O(n·0)), so F_n = F_n^+ ⊕ F_n^- (even and odd parts under the inversion f ↦ f̌). J is the finite étale k-scheme of nonzero 2-torsion points e_i, of degree 3. ℘ ∈ F_2 is non-constant, and ℘' = θ_ξ ℘, where θ_ξ is the invariant derivation attached to ξ. The pair is normalized so that ℘'^2 and ℘^3 have the same leading polar term (ε_6 ℘'^2 = ε_6 ℘^3 = δ^6). This gives relation (28): ℘'^2 = ℘^3 + a_1℘^2 + a_2℘ + a_3.

Proposition 2. The a_α are characterized by the condition (℘^3 + a_1℘^2 + a_2℘ + a_3)|J = 0.
- Necessity: ℘' is odd, and an odd function vanishes at 2-torsion points (2f(x) = 0 and char ≠ 2). So ℘'^2|J = 0.
- Sufficiency: by the previous corollary (Vandermonde, the ℘(e_i) are distinct), 1, ℘, ℘^2 restricted to J ≅ k^3 (after base change) are linearly independent. Hence the linear equation −℘^3|J = a_1 ℘^2|J + a_2 ℘|J + a_3 1|J determines the a_i uniquely.

Corollary 1. The monic cubic X^3 + a_1X^2 + a_2X + a_3 vanishes at the three distinct values ℘(e_i). Hence it equals ∏_{i∈J}(X − ℘(e_i)), i.e. (29), and (−1)^α a_α are the elementary symmetric functions of the ℘(e_i).

Corollary 2. a_1 = 0 iff Tr_{J/k}(℘|J) = Σ℘(e_i) = 0.
- If char k ≠ 3, a constant c has trace 3c ≠ 0 (for c ≠ 0).
- So the trace-zero elements of F_2 form a line W_E complementary to F_1 = k·1_E.
- This gives the canonical splitting (30): F_2 ≅ F_1 ⊕ W_E, with W_E ≅ F_2/F_1 ≅ t_E^{⊗2}. This holds because the fibre of O(0) at the origin is the tangent space t_E.
- The elements of W_E are named 'fonctions de Weierstrass'. The next page puts them in bijection with (t_E^{⊗2})^*.

Purpose. This is an intrinsic, coordinate-free construction of the Weierstrass (Legendre-type) model y^2 = ∏(x − e_i) and of the a_1 = 0 normalization. It serves the later description of F_∞ = k[P,P']/(P'^2 − cubic) and of the modular stack of elliptic curves in char ≠ 2 (the theme of cote 64). Note the normalization: ℘'^2 = ℘^3 + … forces ℘ ~ 4/z^2, i.e. 4 times the classical ℘, so the model is y^2 = cubic rather than y^2 = 4x^3 − g_2x − g_3.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor point: W_E is a 1-dimensional line, and only the suitably scaled elements of W_E satisfy the normalized relation (28) with a_1 = 0. 'Weierstrass functions' must be understood up to the ξ-dependent normalization. The identification W_E ≅ t_E^{⊗2} versus the next page's (t_E^{⊗2})^* depends on whether ξ is taken in t_E or t_E^*; this is a convention, not an error.
The ℘ here is normalized as ≈ 4/z^2 (because ℘'^2 = ℘^3 + …), differing by a factor from the classical Weierstrass ℘. This is consistent but nonstandard.

ideas.what: Characterizing the Weierstrass coefficients a_i by vanishing of the cubic in ℘ on the nonzero 2-torsion points, using that odd functions vanish on E[2]
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass/Legendre model y^2 = (x − e_1)(x − e_2)(x − e_3), roots = x-coordinates of 2-torsion
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Weierstrass, Legendre); standard in Silverman, Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Coefficients of the cubic as elementary symmetric functions of ℘(e_i)
Canonical splitting F_2 = k·1 ⊕ W_E by the trace-zero condition over J (char ≠ 3), with W_E ≅ t_E^{⊗2}
ideas.modern_name: Normalization a_1 = 0 (completing the cube); intrinsic Weierstrass coordinate determined up to ω^{⊗2}; modular-forms weight bookkeeping
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical in coordinates; intrinsic version implicit in Deligne 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire' (1975) and Katz–Mazur (1985)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, intrinsic but entirely classical derivation of the Weierstrass/Legendre equation from 2-torsion. Phrasing via Tr_{J/k} and the line W_E ≅ t_E^{⊗2} is elegant, but it is standard content of the theory of Weierstrass models and modular forms of weight 2.

'il f. et s.' = 'il faut et il suffit'.
